chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of one Kurra of foodstuff. So he bought one Kurra from another man, and said to the man, 'Go and take full payment of your Kurra (from that man).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.اسْتَوْفِ: To take full payment or fulfillment.
key_terms.كُرٌّ: A unit of measurement for grain or foodstuff, used here to denote a specific quantity of debt.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it; it is permissible.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay off a debt by buying goods for the creditor and directing them to collect payment directly?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of 'qard al-bay'' (buying a debt), where a debtor purchases goods from a third party to settle an obligation, allowing the creditor to collect directly from that third party. This ruling highlights the flexibility in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the validity of direct settlement instructions without requiring intermediate handover, thereby facilitating smoother debt resolution.
